spots.name: Winchester Cathedral
spots.summary: Winchester Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of the Holy Trinity and of Saint Peter and Saint Paul and of Saint Swithun in Winchester, is the cathedral of the city of Winchester, England, and is among the largest of its kind in Northern Europe.

names.ja: ウィンチェスター大聖堂

spots.name: Winchester Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Winchester Castle was a royal residence in Winchester, Hampshire, England, founded in 1067 by William the Conqueror. It served as a seat of royal power in the medieval period.

spots.name: New Minster, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The New Minster in Winchester was a royal Benedictine abbey founded in 901 in Winchester in the English county of Hampshire.

spots.name: Wolvesey Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wolvesey Castle, in Winchester, Hampshire, England, was the main residence of the Bishop of Winchester in the Middle Ages. The castle, mostly built by Henry of Blois in the 12th century, is now a ruin, except for its fifteenth-century chapel, which is now part of the bishop's current residence, Wolvesey Palace.

spots.name: Hyde Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hyde Abbey was a medieval Benedictine monastery just outside the walls of Winchester, Hampshire, England. It was dissolved and demolished in 1538 following various acts passed under King Henry VIII to dissolve monasteries and abbeys.

spots.name: Venta Belgarum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Venta Belgarum, or Venta Bulgarum, was a town in the Roman province of Britannia Superior, the civitas capital of the local tribe, the Belgae, and which later became the city of Winchester.

spots.name: Statue of Alfred the Great
spots.summary: The Statue of Alfred the Great is located in the centre of Winchester, England.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of Alfred the Great, Winchester

spots.name: Hospital of St Cross
spots.summary: The Hospital of St Cross and Almshouse of Noble Poverty is a medieval almshouse in Winchester, Hampshire, England. It has been described as "England's oldest and most perfect almshouse". Most of the buildings and grounds are open to the public at certain times. It is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Peninsula Barracks
spots.summary: The Peninsula Barracks are a group of military buildings in Winchester, Hampshire.

spots.name: The Pilgrims' School
spots.summary: The Pilgrims' School is a preparatory school and cathedral school for boys aged 4–13, in the cathedral city Winchester, Hampshire, England.

spots.name: Winchester Guildhall
spots.summary: Winchester Guildhall is a municipal building in the High Street, Winchester, Hampshire. It is a Grade II listed building.

spots.name: King's House, Winchester
spots.summary: The King's House in Winchester was a late 17th-century planned royal palace in the English county of Hampshire. Winchester had been the capital of Wessex and England in Anglo-Saxon times, but became a backwater after the Norman Conquest of England.

spots.name: Westgate
spots.summary: The Westgate is one of two surviving fortified gateways in Winchester, England formerly part of Winchester City Walls. The earliest surviving fabric is of Anglo-Saxon character.

spots.name: Kingsgate
spots.summary: Kingsgate is one of two surviving medieval gates to the city of Winchester, England. The name was first recorded in 1148. The gate is on, or near, the site of one of the Roman gates to the city, and was the entrance to the royal palace before the Cathedral Close was enclosed in the 10th century.

spots.name: St Mary's Abbey, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Mary's Abbey, also known as the Nunnaminster, was a Benedictine nunnery in Winchester, Hampshire, England. It was founded between 899 and 902 by Alfred the Great's widow Ealhswith, who was described as the 'builder' of the Nunnaminster in the New Minster Liber Vitae.

spots.name: Wolvesey Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wolvesey Palace is the residence of the Bishop of Winchester, located in Winchester, England. The bishops had previously lived in the adjacent Wolvesey Castle.

spots.name: The Rifleman's Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Rifleman's Museum is situated at Peninsula Barracks in Winchester, England. The museum is one of several regimental museums that form part of Winchester's Military Museums.

names.ja: 王立グリーン・ジャケッツ連隊博物館

spots.name: St Swithun-upon-Kingsgate Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Swithun upon Kingsgate is a Church of England church in Winchester, Hampshire, England, built in the Middle Ages in the Early English style. Located above the medieval Kingsgate, one of the principal entrances to the city, the church is unusual in forming a part of the fabric of the old city walls.

spots.name: Winchester City Mill
spots.summary: The Winchester City Mill is a restored water mill situated on the River Itchen in the centre of the ancient English city of Winchester. The mill is owned by the National Trust and is a Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: St Catherine's Hill
spots.summary: St. Catherine's Hill is a chalk downland hill and 43-hectare (110-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the outskirts of Winchester in Hampshire, England. It is owned by Winchester College but open to the public.

spots.name: The Gurkha Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Gurkha Museum commemorates the service of Gurkha soldiers to the British Crown, a relationship that has endured since 1815. It is located in Winchester in Hampshire, England and is part of Winchester's Military Museums.

spots.name: Avington Park
spots.summary: Avington House is a 16th-century English country house which stands in Avington Park in the Itchen Valley near Winchester, Hampshire. It is a Grade I listed building.

names.ja: アヴィントン・パーク

spots.name: The Eclipse Inn
spots.summary: The Eclipse Inn is a public house at 25 The Square in the city of Winchester in Hampshire, England. It has been listed Grade II on the National Heritage List for England (NHLE) since January 1974. The building dates from the 16th century and was formerly the rectory of St Lawrence Church.

spots.name: Winchester city walls
spots.summary: Winchester city walls are a series of defensive walls in central Winchester, originally built during the Roman settlement of southern Britain, in what was then the settlement of Venta Belgarum.

spots.name: St Maurice's Church, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Maurice's Church, Winchester was a parish church in the Church of England in Winchester, Hampshire.

spots.name: Hockley Railway Viaduct
spots.summary: The Hockley Railway Viaduct is a disused railway viaduct to the south of Winchester in Hampshire, England.

spots.name: Winchester College War Cloister

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Winchester College War Cloister is a war memorial at Winchester College, in Hampshire, designed by the architect Sir Herbert Baker. The roofed quadrangle is said by Historic England to be the largest known private war memorial in Europe.

spots.name: St Lawrence Church, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Lawrence Church is a parish church in the Church of England in Winchester.

spots.name: St Peter's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Peter's Church is a Roman Catholic church in Winchester, England. It was built in 1924 and designed by Frederick Walters in the Gothic revival style. It is situated on Jewry Street, backing onto St Peter's Street, next to Milner Hall, in the centre of Winchester. It is a Grade II listed building.

spots.name: Castle Hill, Winchester
spots.summary: Castle Hill is a series of buildings used as council offices in Winchester, Hampshire, England. There are two main structures both of which are Grade II listed buildings: the Castle Hill Offices on the east of Castle Avenue and the Castle Avenue Offices on the west of Castle Avenue.

spots.name: Lower Barracks

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lower Barracks was a military installation in Winchester. It was the depot of the Royal Hampshire Regiment from its formation in 1881 until it moved out in 1959. The Royal Hampshire Regiment Museum reopened at Serle's House in 2004. It is one of several independent museums that comprise Winchester's Military Museums.

spots.name: St Bartholomew's Church, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Bartholomew's Church, Winchester is a Church of England parish church in Hyde, Winchester, England.

spots.name: Adjutant General's Corps Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Adjutant General's Corps Museum, also known as The AGC Museum, is a visitor attraction at Peninsula Barracks in Winchester. It displays the history of the Adjutant General's Corps and its antecedents through objects, text, photographs, and dioramas.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of the Adjutant General's Corps

spots.name: St Thomas Church, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Thomas Church is a disused Church of England parish church in Winchester, England.

spots.name: Magdalen Hill Cemetery
spots.summary: Magdalen Hill Cemetery, also known as Morn Hill Cemetery, is a cemetery principally serving the burial requirements of the unparished area of the city of Winchester but located on Magdalen Hill Down in the adjoining civil parish of Chilcomb.

spots.name: Church of the Holy Trinity

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church, Winchester is a Church of England parish church in Winchester, in Hampshire, England.

spots.name: Winchester United Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Winchester United Church is a joint United Reformed and Methodist church in the centre of the city of Winchester in the English county of Hampshire.

spots.name: Twyford Waterworks

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Twyford Waterworks is a preserved pumping station and waterworks situated close to the village of Twyford and the city of Winchester in Hampshire, England. It is a scheduled monument and now operates as a museum. The site is leased by the Twyford Waterworks Trust and is open on selected days during the year.

spots.name: St Mary's Church, Twyford

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Mary's Church, Twyford is a Church of England parish church dedicated to the Virgin Mary in the village of Twyford, Hampshire.

spots.name: Christ Church, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Christ Church, Winchester is a Church of England parish church in Winchester, England. There are approximately 475 members on the electoral roll. It is also in partnership with the diocese of Muhabura and with St Nicholas Church in Kaleerwe, Kampala, both in Uganda.

spots.name: Winchester Science Centre

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Winchester Science Centre is a hands-on educational science, technology centre and research centre located at Morn Hill near Chilcomb, three miles from the city of Winchester in Hampshire, England.

spots.name: Black Rat
spots.summary: The Black Rat was a restaurant in Winchester, in Hampshire, England. As of 2021, the restaurant lost its one star in the Michelin Guide that had been held since 2011. The restaurant closed in 2022.

spots.name: Oram's Arbour
spots.summary: Oram's Arbour was an enclosed settlement (oppidum) during the Iron Age, in what is now Winchester, England. Limited dating evidence suggests the enclosure was dug in the early-mid first century BC.

spots.name: Church of St John the Baptist

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St John the Baptist Church, Winchester is a Grade I Church of England parish church in Winchester, England.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St John the Baptist Church, Winchester

spots.name: Church of St Swithin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Swithun's Church, Martyr Worthy is a Church of England parish church in Martyr Worthy, Hampshire, England.

spots.name: St Peter's Church, Chesil, Winchester

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Peter's Church, Chesil, Winchester, formerly known as St Peter upon Chesille without Eastgate, is a former parish church of the Church of England in Winchester, Hampshire, and is now the home of Chesil Theatre.

spots.name: Corn Exchange
spots.summary: The Corn Exchange, also known as The Arc, is a commercial building in Jewry Street in Winchester, Hampshire, England. The structure, which is currently used as a cultural hub, is a Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: West Hill Cemetery
spots.summary: West Hill Cemetery is a cemetery to the west of the city centre of Winchester in the English county of Hampshire. Opened in the 1840s, the cemetery became the principal place of burial for the city.

spots.name: Winnall Moors
spots.summary: Winnall Moors is a 64-hectare (160-acre) nature reserve in Winchester in Hampshire. It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.
